name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
Information Systems - academic year 21/22
Course Project
Version 1.0.1 - 20/12/2021
Consider the following scenario:

A startup intends to develop a web portal that can help people who intend to organize an event, bringing together in a single website the information concerning the guests and the various services necessary for the event itself to take place.

The platform to be developed envisages the presence of providers and guests, in addition to the organizer.

At registration, providers supply, in addition to their credentials, their personal data and the data of the company they manage (VAT number, company address, accepted payment methods).

The provider, once registered, will be able to enter the services offered by their company, each belonging to a category (catering, hairdresser, florist etc.), each of which will be associated with a virtual showcase in which the provider can upload demonstration photos, together with the corresponding prices and the hours corresponding to the particular service shown by the showcase (e.g. Hairdresser's blow-dry service has as hours 10:00-12:00 from Tuesday to Thursday, Haircut + shampoo service with hours 8:00-12:00 + 15:00-18:00 from Tuesday to Saturday).

The event organizer, identified by their tax code, at registration, in addition to choosing their credentials, will provide their personal data, residence data and their IBAN for the possible payment of the services.

The organizer, through the portal, will be able to create the event, choosing the type of event (wedding, graduation, concert…) to organize, the date, the place where it will be held and the budget planned for the organization of the event. When creating the event the organizer will be able to choose from a pre-existing list the types of service for which they are interested in receiving help (for example catering, flowers, taxi service etc.).

The organizer will also be able to add the guests to the portal, entering the corresponding data, specifying, in addition to the personal data, the email with which the guest will be identified (and which they will use to log in) and the category to which the guest belongs (relative, friend, colleague etc.).

For each guest added, the system will generate an invitation code that will be sent by email to the specified address; this code will be used by the guest as a password to access the portal.

The organizer will also have available a blog associated with their event in which the organizer or the guests can write information about the event, post photos or videos and leave their thoughts by creating new posts or commenting on the existing ones.

The organizer, once the event has been created, will be able to view, for each service chosen when creating the event, the showcases of the providers that supply the chosen type of service and to arrange an appointment compatible with the hours observed by that service, specifying the details and any special requests. The provider, through their interface, will be able to view the various appointment requests and will have to approve them. The approved requests are displayed directly in a calendar on the site associated with the event, where the organizer will be able to consult the appointments for the agreed services.

After the meeting between the provider and the organizer (in which they agree on the details of the service), the provider calculates the quotation and proceeds to upload the amount on the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once the upload has taken place the organizer can choose whether to accept or reject the quotation; if it is accepted, the total amount is subtracted from the remaining budget. By accepting the amount, the organizer chooses the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance or full amount) and the payment method (online or on site). If the payment takes place on site the provider will proceed to confirm the amount paid through the portal (in the case of payment in several instalments the provider confirms the amount of each instalment received).

At any time the organizer will be able to consult the history of the contracts (with the related status and cost) and the budget balance for the entire event.
highLevelGoals: The Event Organizer aims to use the portal to define event details, including type, date, location, and budget, and to select necessary service categories.
The Event Organizer seeks to add guests, categorize them, and have the system generate and send invitation codes for portal access.
The Event Organizer desires to browse provider showcases, arrange appointments for chosen services, and specify special requests.
The Event Organizer aims to accept or reject provider quotations, manage payment modes and methods, and track budget expenditure.
The Event Organizer wants to consult the history of contracts, their status, costs, and the remaining budget for the event at any time.
The Event Organizer aims to utilize an event-associated blog to share information, post media, and interact with guests through posts and comments.
The Provider aims to register on the portal, provide company and personal details, and create virtual showcases for their services with demonstration photos, prices, and availability.
The Provider seeks to view and approve appointment requests from Event Organizers through their interface.
The Provider aims to upload quotations for completed appointments and confirm received payments, including instalment payments, through the portal.
The Guest aims to log in using their invitation code to view event details and participate in the event's blog by creating posts or commenting.
lowLevelGoals: The Event Organizer can initiate the creation of a new event within the portal by providing essential details such as the event type, desired date, and geographical location.
The Event Organizer can set and allocate a budget for the event, allowing for financial planning and tracking.
The Event Organizer can choose from a predefined list of service categories (e.g., catering, photography, venue) that are relevant to their event.
The Event Organizer can modify previously entered event information, such as changing the date, location, or adjusting the budget.
The Event Organizer can manually input guest details (e.g., name, email) to add them to the event's guest list.
The Event Organizer can assign categories to guests, allowing for better organization and targeted communication.
Upon adding a guest, the system automatically creates a unique code that guests can use to access event details on the portal.
The Event Organizer can trigger the system to send the generated invitation codes to guests, typically through email.
The Event Organizer can view a directory of service providers, including their profiles, service offerings, and demonstration photos.
The Event Organizer can refine their search for service providers using various criteria to find suitable options.
The Event Organizer can initiate a request to schedule a meeting or consultation with a selected service provider.
The Event Organizer can include specific instructions or additional information for the service provider during the booking process.
The Event Organizer can access a list of quotations submitted by service providers for requested services.
The Event Organizer can formally agree to the terms and price outlined in a service provider's quotation.
The Event Organizer can formally decline the terms and price outlined in a service provider's quotation.
The Event Organizer can choose how they intend to pay for services from a list of available payment options.
The Event Organizer can proceed with making payments for services based on the accepted quotations and chosen payment methods.
The Event Organizer can view a real-time breakdown of how much of the event budget has been spent and how much remains.
The Event Organizer can access a comprehensive record of all agreements made with service providers for the event.
The Event Organizer can see the current state of each contract, providing an overview of service progress.
The Event Organizer can see the financial details and agreed-upon costs for every service contract.
The Event Organizer can quickly ascertain the unspent portion of their event budget at any given time.
The Event Organizer can compose and publish new articles or updates on the event's dedicated blog.
The Event Organizer can enrich their blog posts by adding visual content to share with guests.
The Event Organizer can see and moderate feedback and discussions from guests on their published blog content.
The Event Organizer can engage with guests by replying to their comments on the event blog.
The Provider can create a new user account by submitting their personal and company information.
The Provider can enter and update information about their business entity.
The Provider can design and populate a dedicated section on the portal to display their service offerings.
The Provider can add visual content to their showcase to illustrate the quality and nature of their services.
The Provider can set and display the costs associated with their various service packages or offerings.
The Provider can mark their availability for bookings, indicating when they are free or occupied.
The Provider can access a dashboard or section showing all incoming requests for appointments.
The Provider can accept a requested appointment, confirming their availability and commitment.
The Provider can decline a requested appointment, indicating unavailability or other reasons.
After an appointment, the Provider can submit a formal price proposal for the services discussed or rendered.
The Provider can mark a service as fully paid once the entire amount has been received.
The Provider can acknowledge and record partial payments received for services.
The Guest can gain access to event-specific information by entering the code provided by the Event Organizer.
Once logged in, the Guest can access all relevant information about the event they are invited to.
The Guest can contribute to the event's blog by publishing their own content or updates.
The Guest can interact with content on the event blog by leaving comments on posts made by the organizer or other guests.
